newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Feb 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Feb 3.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Thai paramilitary forces have fought a gunbattle with members of a breakaway ethnic Karen group which crossed the border into Thailand from Burma in a bid to launch an attack on the Karen National Union . The brief shootout took place yesterday on the Thai-Burmese border in Tak province and the Thai side managed to halt the advance of the Democratic Karen Buddhist Army. (THE NATION)

- Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh will tomorrow ask the Cabinet to approve the establishment of the administrative court instead of waiting for the Constitution Drafting Assembly to decide the new court's structure. The Solidarity Party is expected to be brought into the coalition in the event that the Social Action Party pulls out as a result of the conflict over the administrative court. (THE NATION, BANGKOK POST)

- Constitution drafting committee chairman Anand Panyarachun is hopeful that his committee will finish its work within the time limit set. However, he thinks that the draft may not be as good as it could be due to the time pressure. He has also warned the mass media not to confuse the public over what the new constitution would be like. (THE NATION)

- The Industrial Finance Corporation of Thailand (IFCT) has agreed in principle to assume responsibility for the rehabilitation of the ailing Bangkok Bank of Commerce (BBC), says governor of the Bank of Thailand. He says the IFCT is conducting a feasibility study for the purpose of developing financial and operational rehabilitation plans for BBC.

- Siam Cement Plc will have to wait until the end of this year to find out whether Vietnam is able to provide limestone sources for the company to proceed with cement production in Ho Chi Minh City. The firm is waiting for the Vietnamese authorities to complete the survey to find an available sources of limestone suitable for production of cement. (BUSINESS DAY)

- Thailand will join Singapore and Malaysia in battling European Union claims that they are dumping facsimile machines on EU members. This month the EU is likely to announce an investigation into alleged dumping by Thailand. (BANGKOK POST)
